evidence: Receiving DO2 sensors 50.0–52.0 h: 6.47, 6.30, 6.18, 6.25, 6.34, 6.10, 5.96, 6.06, 6.26, 5.90 mg/L — sustained low plateau after a ~6 mg/L step drop at t=50.2 h
Source batches at 50–52 h: 10.4–11.5 mg/L (all three), showing the receiving behavior is anomalous, not a shared seasonal/trajectory effect
Receiving P assay: 0.0347 g/L @12 h, 0.0 @24 h, 0.963 @36 h, 2.654 g/L @48 h — source-comparable production, so feed reduction would sacrifice yield unnecessarily
minimum_do_mg_l = 2.0; current DO ~6 mg/L, still above constraint but downward margin eroding; allowed_actions: increase_air scales air 1.0→1.15 with feed retained at 1.0
args.rationale: At t=52 h the receiving vessel's DO2 dropped abruptly from ~12 mg/L to ~5.9–6.5 mg/L (all readings 50.2–52.0 h are ~6), unlike all three source batches which remained at ~10–11 mg/L at the same age. This indicates a sudden oxygen-demand surge. Because product accumulation (P ≈ 2.65 g/L at 48 h) is on track with source batches, the priority is to restore oxygen supply without sacrificing product mass. increase_air (+15% aeration, feed unchanged) directly addresses the oxygen deficit, preserves full feed/product trajectory, and raises DO headroom well away from the 2.0 mg/L constraint. reduce_feed would lower demand but cuts substrate and risks product-mass loss; combined adds feed cut that is unnecessary given DO is still ~3x above minimum; strong_feed_reduction risks even greater yield loss; stop yields zero counted production. If DO were falling toward 2 mg/L or below, the bounded combined action would be the fallback, but current DO (~6 mg/L) supports aeration-only correction.
args.uncertainty: Hidden receiving parameters are unknown; DO trend beyond 52 h is unobserved, so it is uncertain whether demand will continue rising (which could later require combined/stronger action) or re-equilibrate. Aeration response kinetics (+15% upper bound) are also uncertain — if the demand surge exceeds transfer capacity gained, DO could continue to fall. Assay data are 4 h stale (P at 48 h); current product state could be lower than inferred. No extra assay was requested because the DO sensor (online) already provides the operative signal and the assay would not change the oxygen-management choice.
